result.topic_en: The page holds reprinted unsolved questions: the end of a question by A. Astor on tangents converging to the real inflexion point of a curve, question 1672 by Barisien on the pedal of a sextic and an area ratio, question 1686 by Lucien Lévy on a system of 2n−1 equations, and the beginning of question 1687.

1672 (1894, 4*). — La podaire du centre de la courbe
$4(x^2+y^2-a^2)^3+27a^2x^4=0$
a pour équation
$4(x^2+y^3)^3-a^2(2x^2+y^3)^2=0.$
La rapport de l'aire de la première courbe à celle de la seconde est $\frac{15}{19}$. E.-N. BARISIEN.

1686 (1895, 33*). — Résoudre les $2n-1$ équations à $2n-1$ inconnues
$\frac{1}{2}=\mathrm{X}_1x_1 + \ldots + \mathrm{X}_{n-1}x_{n-1}[?] + \mathrm{X}_n,$
$\frac{1}{3}=\mathrm{X}_1x_1^2 + \ldots + \mathrm{X}_{n-1}x_{n-1}^2 + \mathrm{X}_n,$
. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .,
$\frac{1}{2n}=\mathrm{X}_1x_1^{2n-1} + \ldots + \mathrm{X}_{n-1}x_{n-1}^{2n-1} + \mathrm{X}_n,$
et montrer que les inconnues $x_1, \ldots, x_{n-1}$ sont les racines, autres que zéro et un, de l'équation
$\frac{\partial^{n-1}\lambda^n(\lambda-1)^n}{\partial\lambda^{n-1}}=0.$
LUCIEN LÉVY.

1687 (1895, 33*). — On sait que l'équation
$\frac{\partial^n x^n(x-1)^n}{\partial x^n}=0$

questions.author: E.-N. Barisien
questions.statement_fr:
La podaire du centre de la courbe
$4(x^2+y^2-a^2)^3+27a^2x^4=0$
a pour équation
$4(x^2+y^3)^3-a^2(2x^2+y^3)^2=0.$
La rapport de l'aire de la première courbe à celle de la seconde est $\frac{15}{19}$.
questions.statement_en:
The pedal with respect to the centre of the curve
$4(x^2+y^2-a^2)^3+27a^2x^4=0$
has the equation
$4(x^2+y^3)^3-a^2(2x^2+y^3)^2=0.$
The ratio of the area of the first curve to that of the second is $\frac{15}{19}$.

questions.author: Lucien Lévy
questions.statement_fr:
Résoudre les $2n-1$ équations à $2n-1$ inconnues
$\frac{1}{2}=\mathrm{X}_1x_1 + \ldots + \mathrm{X}_{n-1}x_{n-1}[?] + \mathrm{X}_n,$
$\frac{1}{3}=\mathrm{X}_1x_1^2 + \ldots + \mathrm{X}_{n-1}x_{n-1}^2 + \mathrm{X}_n,$
. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .,
$\frac{1}{2n}=\mathrm{X}_1x_1^{2n-1} + \ldots + \mathrm{X}_{n-1}x_{n-1}^{2n-1} + \mathrm{X}_n,$
et montrer que les inconnues $x_1, \ldots, x_{n-1}$ sont les racines, autres que zéro et un, de l'équation
$\frac{\partial^{n-1}\lambda^n(\lambda-1)^n}{\partial\lambda^{n-1}}=0.$
questions.statement_en:
Solve the $2n-1$ equations in $2n-1$ unknowns
$\frac{1}{2}=\mathrm{X}_1x_1 + \ldots + \mathrm{X}_{n-1}x_{n-1} + \mathrm{X}_n,$
$\frac{1}{3}=\mathrm{X}_1x_1^2 + \ldots + \mathrm{X}_{n-1}x_{n-1}^2 + \mathrm{X}_n,$
...,
$\frac{1}{2n}=\mathrm{X}_1x_1^{2n-1} + \ldots + \mathrm{X}_{n-1}x_{n-1}^{2n-1} + \mathrm{X}_n,$
and show that the unknowns $x_1, \ldots, x_{n-1}$ are the roots, other than zero and one, of the equation
$\frac{\partial^{n-1}\lambda^n(\lambda-1)^n}{\partial\lambda^{n-1}}=0.$

questions.statement_fr:
On sait que l'équation
$\frac{\partial^n x^n(x-1)^n}{\partial x^n}=0$
questions.statement_en:
It is known that the equation
$\frac{\partial^n x^n(x-1)^n}{\partial x^n}=0$

result.notes_en: There is no editorial text on this page apart from the page number (238). The second equation in question 1672 is printed with $y^3$, probably a misprint for $y^2$, and is transcribed as printed. In the first equation of question 1686, the subscript of the last $x$ is printed defectively and appears as 'n 1'; it is transcribed as $x_{n-1}$ with [?].
